          Arsenal v Everton Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Jonathan Burnett / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to this Premier League match at the Emirates Stadium with our Arsenal vs Everton prediction and preview. Will the Gunners overcome an Everton side who suffered their first league loss of the season last week?

The Premier League table is starting to take shape as champions Arsenal return to domestic action, hosting Everton at the Emirates following a 2–2 draw with Bayern Munich in their midweek Champions League clash.

Declan Rice rescued a point for the Gunners eight minutes from time after Eberechi Eze had given them a first-half lead at Allianz Arena, with Bayern bouncing back via goals from Alphonso Davies and Harry Kane.

Viktor Gyökeres came off the bench to assist Rice's equaliser, and with Eze replacing Bukayo Saka early on before scoring in the 25th minute, no Premier League side this season has more goal contributions from substitutes in all competitions than Arsenal's nine (five goals, four assists).

Domestically, Arsenal have bounced back from their 3–0 defeat at Brighton just before the latest international break, with one-goal wins over Leeds United and Nottingham Forest. But the defending champions failed to truly convince in either of those victories.

Second-half strikes from Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimarães earned Arsenal a 2–1 comeback victory over Leeds in their last home league outing. They then needed a deflected 80th-minute goal from Noni Madueke to seal a 1–0 win at the City Ground last weekend.

Set up by a league-leading fourth assist of the season from Rice, Madueke became the third substitute in a row to score the decisive goal in a Premier League game for Arsenal, after Guimarães also came on to net late winners against Sunderland and Leeds.

The Gunners have ground to make up on Manchester City at the summit and could trail Enzo Maresca's side by six points once they kick-off as the leaders face Aston Villa in Saturday's early kick-off. Everton sit eighth, six places and eight points further back.

The Toffees also made a strong start to their campaign and were fifth after two wins and four draws in their first six games, but their unbeaten run came to an end in a 2–0 home defeat to Chelsea last time out.
They didn't do much to help their cause, with only six shots in total, their fewest in a Premier League game since hitting just five against Arsenal in December 2025.
Goals could indeed be at a premium in this game, given Arsenal and Everton have recorded the joint-most 1-0 wins (32 each) in the Premier League since Arteta was hired by Arsenal in December 2019.
However, recent form also suggests Arsenal have good reason to be confident having won 11 of their last 12 Premier League games, including six from six at the Emirates over the course of that run.
Everton, meanwhile, have won just one of their last 30 Premier League away games against Arsenal, a 1–0 victory in the behind-closed-doors 2020-21 season under Carlo Ancelotti.

Across David Moyes' two spells, the Toffees have never enjoyed victory in 13 attempts at Highbury or the Emirates, losing on 10 occasions, while the Scot has lost 11 of his last 12 Premier League matches against the reigning champions.

In terms of team news, Arsenal are still without William Saliba for the long term, and Saka has joined him and Christos Tzolis in the treatment room after injuring his thigh in Wednesday's 2–2 draw in Munich. Piero Hincapié‘s ankle is being assessed ahead of a potential return at left-back.

Everton, meanwhile, have a fully fit squad to choose from at the time of writing after Christian Nørgaard – who moved from Arsenal while carrying an injury over the summer – finally made his Toffees debut off the bench against Chelsea.
Everton's dismal record against Arsenal didn't let up last season, with Moyes' side losing 1–0 and 2–0 respectively in December (at home) and March (at the Emirates).

Arsenal come into this game unbeaten in their last seven against Everton in the Premier League – winning five – which is their best run against the Toffees since going 13 without defeat between December 2007 and December 2013.
The Opta supercomputer is in little doubt when it comes to predicting the outcome of this game, with Arsenal understandably seen as overwhelming favourites.
Across 10,000 pre-match simulations, the Gunners came away with victory in 69.5% of the outcomes, suggesting there'll be a very expectant home crowd at the Emirates.
